transcript.content: Hello, I'm glad you're here today. What brings you in to see me?
To be honest, I'm mostly here because my family insisted. I just can't shake this constant fear of putting on weight, so I keep cutting back on what I eat even though they say I'm already too thin.
Do you ever experience episodes where you feel out of control and eat a very large amount of food in a short time, followed by trying to get rid of it, such as by making yourself throw up?
No, I've never done anything like that or made myself throw up. I actually do the opposite—I just try to restrict my food and eat as little as possible. I never lose control or overeat.
Could you please share your current height and weight with me?
I don't know my exact weight off the top of my head right now. I also haven't had my height measured recently, so I'm not entirely sure of the exact numbers.
If you menstruate, have you noticed your periods becoming irregular or stopping altogether since you started restricting your food?
Actually, I'm a man, so I don't menstruate. That isn't something I've ever had to deal with.
Have you noticed a significant decrease in your sex drive or any changes in your sexual function since you started restricting your food?
Honestly, I haven't really thought about that or noticed any changes. I've been so focused on my work and managing everything at home lately that it hasn't really crossed my mind.
Even if you don't know the exact numbers, could you estimate about how much weight you have lost since you started restricting your food?

I'm really not sure of the exact amount of weight I've lost because I don't keep track of the total number. I just know that my pants are hanging off me now and my wedding ring has gotten really loose.
Since you started restricting your food and losing weight, have you experienced any new difficulties with achieving or maintaining an erection?
I haven't really noticed any issues with that. It's not something I've paid much attention to lately.
Do you remember what your weight was before you started restricting your food, or what your typical weight used to be?
I don't remember the exact numerical weight I was before I started cutting back on food. I just know that I've lost enough for my pants to hang off me now and my wedding ring to feel pretty loose.
When you look at yourself in the mirror, do you still feel that you are overweight or too fat, even though your clothes are hanging off you?

My clothes and wedding ring are definitely loose, but when I look in the mirror, I don't see myself as fat—I actually feel a sense of pride in looking lean and "shredded." Still, I have this constant, intense fear that I'll balloon up overnight if I let my guard down, which is why I keep pushing myself. I honestly think my family is overreacting about me being too thin, since to me, this is just about being highly disciplined.
Compared to before you started restricting your food, would you say your actual interest in sex or intimacy has decreased, even if you've been busy with work?
I'm not really sure, to be honest. I've just been so exhausted lately and focused on keeping up with my work at the shop and my daily routine that I haven't given it much thought.
Have you noticed yourself feeling unusually cold even when others are comfortable, or experiencing dizziness when you stand up?

I do feel cold pretty much all the time now, and I've had some lightheaded spells and even passed out a couple of times at the shop. But honestly, I think my wife and the doctors are overreacting to it, because to me it's just a sign of my hard work and discipline.
Since you mentioned that doctors have been involved, do you remember what weight they recorded at your recent visit, or do you know your current height?
I don't remember the exact weight the doctor recorded at my visit, and I'm not entirely sure of my exact height either. I just know that my weight has definitely been going down lately.
Have you noticed a decrease or complete absence of your usual morning erections since you began losing weight?
I can't say I've paid much attention to that or really noticed a difference. Lately, I'm just so drained from my busy routine and managing what I eat that it's the last thing on my mind.
Since you mentioned seeing doctors recently, did they run any blood tests and mention if your hormone levels, such as testosterone, were low?
I don't recall if they ran those specific blood tests or mentioned anything about my hormone or testosterone levels. Everything was a bit of a blur at that appointment, so I'm really not sure.
